BiblicalUsage: Chamiyshiy is the fifth, the ordinal, and it marks days, portions, and offerings. The evening and the morning were the fifth day, Joseph set the fifth part of Egypt's increase for Pharaoh, a man who harmed a holy thing adds the fifth part to his amends, and on the fifth day Shelumiel brought his offering for Simeon.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the fifth part teaches me that making things right costs more than the damage done. Restitution adds a fifth on top, because repentance is not only repaying what was taken but honouring the one it was taken from.
